one_sentence_story_promise: This is the story of how an office subleasing company convinced Wall Street and the world's most aggressive tech investor it was an ethereal software platform, reached a $47 billion valuation, and then ran out of money in 33 days after being forced to file its real accounting paperwork with the SEC.
central_question: How did sophisticated banks, sovereign wealth funds, and Silicon Valley's biggest checkbook mistake commercial office rent for a software revolution?
viewer_payoff: By the end, the viewer will understand the exact financial alchemy—specifically the asset-liability duration mismatch, invented accounting metrics like 'Community Adjusted EBITDA', and SoftBank's blitzscaling incentives—that allowed WeWork to disguise an ancient, low-margin real estate landlord business as an infinite-multiple tech monopoly.
editorial_tone: Dry, forensic, comedic investigative documentary. The smart friend who actually read the 200-page S-1 filing so you don't have to.
